questions.question: Which patient populations are at an increased risk of spine infection?
questions.detail: Populations at higher risk include those with diabetes, intravenous drug users, and individuals who have undergone previous spinal surgical procedures.

questions.question: Adult hematogenous spine infection typically starts in which location?
choices: The center of the nucleus pulposus
questions.detail: In adults, hematogenous spread of infection usually originates at the vertebral body endplate.

questions.question: Why does adult discitis/osteomyelitis typically involve two adjacent vertebrae and the intervening disc?
choices: The disc has its own separate blood supply
A single segmental artery supplies two adjacent segmental endplates
The anterior longitudinal ligament carries the infection
questions.detail: This involvement occurs because a single segmental artery provides the blood supply to two adjacent segmental endplates.

questions.question: What is the optimal imaging modality for suspected discitis/osteomyelitis?
questions.detail: MRI is considered the optimal imaging modality for diagnosing suspected discitis/osteomyelitis.

questions.question: What is the most sensitive MR imaging sign for detecting a spinal infection?
questions.detail: The most sensitive indicator of spinal infection on MRI is the presence of paraspinal or epidural inflammatory changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic MRI finding of discitis/osteomyelitis?
choices: Erosion or destruction of vertebral endplates
Fluid signal within the disc space
Edema evident across the disc space
questions.detail: Key MRI features include endplate destruction, disc enhancement, fluid signal in the disc space, and edema spanning the disc.

questions.question: In the epidural space, an infection that is 'centrally necrotic' is defined as an:
questions.detail: A centrally necrotic infection within the epidural space is classified as an abscess.

questions.question: Why is 'fat suppression' an extremely helpful technique for detecting early epidural infection?
choices: It suppresses the normal hyperintense signal of epidural fat on T1, making enhancement more conspicuous
It allows for the measurement of the disc-space height
It distinguishes between pus and blood
It is only helpful in children
questions.detail: Fat suppression is useful because it removes the bright T1 signal of normal epidural fat, making abnormal contrast enhancement easier to see.

questions.question: Tuberculous osteomyelitis of the spine is also known as:
questions.detail: Pott disease is the eponym for tuberculous osteomyelitis involving the spine.

questions.question: How does Pott disease typically differ from pyogenic discitis regarding the intervertebral discs?
choices: The discs are the first structures destroyed
The discs are usually spared because M. tuberculosis lacks proteolytic enzymes
There is no difference; they appear identical
questions.detail: In Pott disease, intervertebral discs are typically spared because Mycobacterium tuberculosis does not possess proteolytic enzymes.

questions.question: A 'gibbus deformity' is a classic complication of Pott disease and is defined as:
choices: A lateral curvature of the spine
An acutely angled kyphosis due to wedge-shaped anterior vertebral compression
A complete dissolution of the posterior elements
A widening of the spinal canal
questions.detail: A gibbus deformity is an acutely angled kyphosis resulting from wedge-shaped compression of the anterior vertebral body.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of patients with Pott disease also have active pulmonary tuberculosis?
questions.detail: Only about 10% of patients diagnosed with Pott disease present with concurrent active pulmonary tuberculosis.

questions.question: Facet septic arthritis should be suspected when the degree of periarticular inflammatory change is:
choices: Exactly equal to the degree of disc degeneration
Out of proportion to a relatively milder degree of joint degeneration
Only seen in the cervical spine
questions.detail: The diagnosis is suspected when inflammatory changes are significantly greater than what would be expected for the degree of joint degeneration present.

questions.question: On CT, the earliest sign of discitis/osteomyelitis is typically:
choices: Dense sclerosis of the vertebral body
Osseous erosion or destruction of the endplates
questions.detail: The initial sign seen on CT scans for these infections is usually the erosion or destruction of the bone at the vertebral endplates.

questions.question: Infection originating in the psoas muscle that spreads to the disc space is an example of spread between which two compartments?
questions.detail: This represents the spread of infection between the retroperitoneum/psoas compartment and the disc/vertebral body compartment.
